criterion.text: The paper studies scheduling or control policies for entanglement distribution that are derived by optimization (an MDP or linear-programming formulation) and evaluates them against a simple heuristic or index policy.

parts.name: optimal scheduling policy
parts.definition: The paper itself formulates and solves a scheduling or control problem for entanglement distribution as a Markov decision process or linear program (or an equivalent optimization) and obtains an optimal or near-optimal policy; merely mentioning optimization does not meet it.

parts.name: heuristic or index policy
parts.definition: The paper itself defines or evaluates a simple heuristic, greedy, myopic, threshold or index policy (such as a Whittle or max-weight index) and compares its performance to the optimal policy, for entanglement distribution.

parts.name: age or fidelity penalty
parts.definition: The paper examines how the policy performance or gap depends on the form of an age-of-information or fidelity/decoherence penalty function.

parts.name: delayed channel state information
parts.definition: The paper analyzes the effect of delayed, outdated or partial channel state information on the scheduling policies.

parts.name: time-varying Markov channel
parts.definition: The paper models the link or channel as time-varying, such as a Markov or Gilbert-Elliott channel, and studies its effect on policy performance.

queries.label: Query 1
queries.query_text: ("entanglement distribution" OR "quantum networks" OR "quantum switch") AND (scheduling OR "markov decision process" OR "whittle index")
